briefing.headline: Midterms, budgets and party shifts dominate politics today
briefing.overview: US midterm campaigning intensifies as leaders host town‑halls and the DOJ charges alleged illegal voters. In the UK the Chancellor rejects a tax rise while Welsh politics sees defections and budget debates.

stories.title: Chancellor rejects Capital Gains Tax rise
stories.what_happened: The Chancellor announced the Budget will not increase Capital Gains Tax, despite Labour calls to equalise it with income tax. Critics warn the decision could keep wealthy investors in Britain.
stories.why_it_matters: The story illustrates executive fiscal decision‑making and the tension between government and opposition over tax policy, a key A‑level theme. It also touches on the principle of fiscal autonomy within the UK constitution.

perspectives.label: Supporters argue
perspectives.text: Keeping CGT unchanged maintains the UK's attractiveness for investment and avoids capital flight.

perspectives.label: Critics argue
perspectives.text: Not raising CGT perpetuates inequality and misses an opportunity for progressive revenue.

perspectives.label: From the right
perspectives.text: A lower CGT aligns with free‑market principles and encourages entrepreneurship.

key_term.definition: A tax on the profit made when an asset is sold for more than its purchase price.

stories.exam_use: Use as evidence in an essay on the executive’s role in fiscal policy and opposition challenges.

stories.title: Two Labour councillors join Plaid Cymru
stories.what_happened: Two Labour councillors in Monmouthshire defected to Plaid Cymru, leaving the ruling coalition with fewer seats. The move shifts the local balance of power in the council.
stories.why_it_matters: The incident shows party realignment at sub‑national level and the impact of defections on coalition stability, relevant to the AQA study of political parties and devolution.

perspectives.label: Supporters argue
perspectives.text: Defections reflect genuine policy disagreements and give voters clearer choices.

perspectives.label: Critics argue
perspectives.text: Frequent party switching can undermine voter trust in party commitments.

perspectives.label: From the left
perspectives.text: The shift may strengthen regional nationalist representation.

key_term.definition: When an elected representative leaves one political party to join another.

stories.exam_use: Cite as a case study of party dynamics and coalition politics in Wales.

stories.title: DOJ charges 28 alleged non‑citizen voters in California
stories.what_happened: The US Department of Justice announced charges against 28 California voters alleged to be non‑citizens. The charges were part of a broader investigation into voter fraud.
stories.why_it_matters: The case highlights enforcement of election laws and debates over voter eligibility, linking to the A‑level focus on electoral integrity and the role of the courts.

perspectives.label: Supporters argue
perspectives.text: Strict enforcement protects the legitimacy of elections.

perspectives.label: Critics argue
perspectives.text: Targeting voters may discourage participation and raise civil‑rights concerns.

perspectives.label: From the left
perspectives.text: The action could be seen as a tool of voter suppression.

key_term.definition: Illegitimate interference with the electoral process, such as voting by ineligible persons.

stories.exam_use: Use to discuss the balance between election security and civil liberties in a US politics essay.

stories.title: Kamala Harris and NAACP host midterm town halls
stories.what_happened: Former Vice President Kamala Harris and the NAACP announced a series of town‑hall events aimed at mobilising voters in swing states ahead of the 2026 midterms. The effort is linked to speculation about Harris’s 2028 presidential ambitions.
stories.why_it_matters: The initiative illustrates how pressure groups and political figures seek to influence voter turnout, a key topic in the AQA unit on pressure groups and electoral participation.

perspectives.label: Supporters argue
perspectives.text: Town halls increase civic engagement and inform voters about key issues.

perspectives.label: Critics argue
perspectives.text: The events may be partisan tools to sway undecided voters.

perspectives.label: From the right
perspectives.text: Such mobilisation can be seen as unnecessary government‑linked campaigning.

key_term.definition: An organised group that seeks to influence public policy without seeking electoral office.

stories.exam_use: Reference when evaluating the impact of interest groups on electoral outcomes.

stories.title: SCOTUS to hear major free‑exercise case
stories.what_happened: The US Supreme Court scheduled oral arguments for 3 Nov on St. Mary Catholic Parish v. Roy, a case concerning the free‑exercise clause of the Constitution. The ruling could expand religious‑rights jurisprudence.
stories.why_it_matters: The case exemplifies judicial review of constitutional rights, linking to A‑level study of the US courts and the separation of powers.

perspectives.label: Supporters argue
perspectives.text: A broader interpretation protects religious freedom.

perspectives.label: Critics argue
perspectives.text: Expanding rights may undermine secular law and equal treatment.

perspectives.label: From the left
perspectives.text: The decision could affect minority religious groups and social equity.

key_term.definition: Part of the First Amendment that prohibits the government from interfering with religious practices.

stories.exam_use: Use as evidence when discussing judicial influence on constitutional rights.

compare.uk: The UK Prime Minister, as head of the executive, is accountable to Parliament and can be questioned at PMQs, showing a fused executive‑legislature relationship.
compare.us: The US President operates under a separation of powers, with limited direct accountability to Congress, as highlighted by the SCOTUS discussion of executive‑legislative boundaries.
compare.insight: The contrast demonstrates how the UK’s parliamentary system blends executive and legislative functions, whereas the US system maintains distinct, checks‑and‑balances‑driven branches.

ideas_lens.text: United Airlines CEO Scott Kirby’s call for a wealth and inheritance tax reflects liberal ideas about using state intervention to promote economic fairness, echoing John Stuart Mill’s advocacy for redistribution to correct market failures.

exam_question.question: Assess the extent to which the executive’s fiscal decisions are constrained by opposition parties in the UK and the US.
exam_question.tip: Compare the Chancellor’s Budget decision with the US President’s limited fiscal powers, using recent examples.
